author: human
request:
Feature request: visits can currently only be created, never corrected. Two
product decisions come with it, made here as the product owner:

- Non-goal NG-5 is narrowed: cancelling a booked visit stays out of scope,
  but correcting its date and description is now in. Record the narrowing
  the way the project records non-goal changes.
- The edit form is reachable by its URL alone: the owner detail page gains
  no edit link in this request. A visible entry point may come as a
  follow-up request.

Add editing for a booked visit:

- GET /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits/{visitId}/edit shows the visit
  form prefilled with that visit's current date and description. Reuse the
  existing visit form template (pets/createOrUpdateVisitForm) and its `visit`
  model attribute.
- POST to the same URL validates like visit creation (description required,
  date in the future). On success it updates that visit in place — the pet
  must not gain an additional visit record — and redirects to the owner
  detail page. On validation failure it redisplays the form.

Cover the new behavior with tests.

These are all the product decisions; no further product answer will come
during the work. Where a choice still seems open, take the narrowest reading
consistent with this request and record the open question rather than
waiting.

author: product-requirements-expert
title: Staff can correct a booked visit's date and description
summary: A booked visit's date and description can be corrected under the same rules as booking. The correction updates that visit in place, never adding another, and returns to the owner's record. The correction form is reachable by its address alone.
acceptance_criteria: given a booked visit, when GET /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits/{visitId}/edit is requested, then the existing visit form (pets/createOrUpdateVisitForm) is shown with its `visit` model attribute prefilled with that visit's current date and description

given a booked visit, when a description and a date later than today are POSTed to the same URL, then that visit is updated in place, the pet's visit count is unchanged, and the response redirects to the owner detail page
given a booked visit, when a correction with a blank description is POSTed, then the form is redisplayed with an error on the description and the stored visit is unchanged
given a booked visit, when a correction with a date of today or earlier is POSTed, then the form is redisplayed with an error on the date and the stored visit is unchanged
given a visit id that does not belong to the named pet or does not exist, when its correction form is requested or submitted, then the request is refused and no visit is changed
non_goals: an edit link or any visible entry point on the owner detail page (owner deferred to a possible follow-up request)
changing which pet a visit belongs to
a confirmation message after a successful correction (not requested; recorded as an open question)
notes: NG-5 narrowed per the intake decision; new non-goal ADR docs/adr/2026-10-25-non-goal-visit-cancellation-only.md, and the 2026-08-08 non-goal ADR status now names the amendment. The ADR index row in docs/adr/README.md is outside this agent's write scope: system-design-expert should add it. Narrowest readings taken and recorded under PRD Open Questions: a past-dated visit is correctable only by moving it forward (same date rule as booking); no confirmation message; no entry-point link. The foreign/missing-visit refusal mirrors Visits edge case 1 for booking. Autofix audit: no prd-autofix records.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: Visit correction is a second route pair on VisitController in the owner package (system-design § Contracts, VisitController row), on the Owner -> Pet -> Visit aggregate path with OwnerRepository as the sole write path (§ Contracts, Invariants paragraph). The adjustments: Pet gains a lookup of one of its visits by identity, mirroring Owner.getPet(Integer) (Owner.java:126); the controller's `visit` model attribute branches on an optional `visitId` path variable, the pattern PetController.findPet uses (PetController.java:76-77, `@PathVariable(name=..., required=false)`); the non-future-date check is extracted once and shared by both POST handlers. The template already posts to its own URL (no form action), so it is reused unchanged. No new module, dependency, or bounded context. NG-5 is narrowed by the new non-goal ADR; nothing in durable memory conflicts. Basis: grep and file reads (IDE oracle not connected).
integration_points: Binding target, GET and POST /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits/{visitId}/edit: the persisted Visit loaded through owner.getPet(petId) and then the pet's lookup by visitId, behind an allow-list. The controller's @InitBinder keeps setDisallowedFields("id", "*.id") (security-principles § Mass assignment) and adds setAllowedFields("date", "description"), the only fields the form offers; this also applies to the booking route and does not change it (system-design § Threat Model, mass-assignment row)

Double for the repository boundary: the existing @MockitoBean OwnerRepository fixture in VisitControllerTests, which the suite already uses. The owner fixture gains a pet carrying one persisted visit with an id. Assert in-place update by capturing the saved Owner (or verifying save) and checking the pet's visit count and the visit's new date and description. A hand-written double is preferred per testing-principles but not required, since the seam is already Mockito-based
Double for the framework transport: MockMvc (the sanctioned mock, CLAUDE.md Testing Strategy)

Persistence: the POST handler saves the same Owner instance placed in the model by the model-attribute method. Its graph holds the bound visit, so merge cascades the update and inserts nothing (system-design § Contracts, Invariants paragraph)

patterns.description: identity lookup over an eagerly fetched child collection, skipping unsaved entries: the template for Pet's visit lookup
optional path variable on a shared @ModelAttribute method, so one method serves both the create and edit routes
refusal of a foreign or missing owner or pet with IllegalArgumentException; a missing or foreign visit is refused the same way (PRD Visits edge case 3 mirrors edge case 1)

risks.risk: The current @ModelAttribute("visit") method creates a new Visit and attaches it to the pet on every request to the controller. Left unchanged on the edit routes, the save would cascade a blank extra visit and break 'the pet gains no further visit'
risks.mitigation: When visitId is present, the model-attribute method returns the pet's existing visit, or refuses, and never creates or attaches a new Visit. The new-visit branch runs only when visitId is absent. A test asserts the pet's visit count is unchanged after a correction (system-design § Contracts, Invariants paragraph)

risks.risk: The non-future-date rule copied into a second handler would be a new controller rule, a fresh breach of the Web controller row (architecture-principles § Pattern catalog, paragraph on controllers carrying rules)
risks.mitigation: Extract the existing check into one private method of VisitController that both POST handlers call. It is the same rule the recorded deviation already names, kept in one place; the VisitController Contracts row now records that one check serves both

risks.risk: A visit id belonging to another pet, or to a pet of another owner, must not be readable or writable through this pet's URL (PRD Visits edge case 3)
risks.mitigation: Look the visit up only among the pet's own visits, where the pet itself was found through the owner from the URL. Absent means refused with IllegalArgumentException, as for a foreign pet. Test both GET and POST, and assert no save on POST (security-principles § Trust Boundaries, external input row)

risks.risk: A failed validation must leave the stored visit unchanged
risks.mitigation: open-in-view is disabled and the controller holds no transaction, so the bound visit is detached and changes persist only through owners.save. Return the form before any save on errors, and verify that save is never called in the failure tests (system-design § Persistence)

risks.risk: Visit lookup path scales with the pet's visit count (system-design § Scale and Load, 'Visit lookup for correction' row)
risks.mitigation: Simplest readable form: a linear scan over the eagerly fetched visits

risks.risk: New user-facing text such as an 'Update Visit' button label would need keys in all eleven bundles (REQ-LANG-002, enforced by the bundle-key test)
risks.mitigation: Narrowest reading: reuse the template unchanged. Its heading already drops 'New' for a persisted visit. A relabelled button is outside this slice; if one is added, add the key to every bundle

notes: Autofix audit: no design-doc-autofix records in the log. Design-doc writes this dispatch: docs/system-design.md (REQ-VIS-003 added to the Pet, Visit, OwnerRepository, and VisitController Contracts rows; an Invariants sentence on reaching and correcting a visit, back-linked to the new non-goal ADR; the Security Context inputs line gains visit identifiers; the mass-assignment Threat Model row gains the visit allow-list; a new § Scale and Load section with the visit-lookup row, since the doc had no such section). docs/adr/README.md: index row added for 2026-10-25-non-goal-visit-cancellation-only.md, and the 2026-08-08 row's status now records the NG-5 amendment, matching that ADR's Status line. No architectural ADR: the slice reuses existing patterns and constrains no future slice beyond what the non-goal ADR records. The 2026-08-08 ADR is on origin/agent-team, so amending it rather than editing it in place is correct. The two non-goal ADR files and docs/prd.md were written by product-requirements-expert (prd-entry line 3), not by this dispatch. Success redirects to /owners/{ownerId} with no flash message, per the prd-entry non-goals.

author: security-reviewer
approved_aspects: Ownership scoping (PRD Visits edge case 3): the edit routes resolve the visit only through owners.findById(ownerId) -> owner.getPet(petId) -> pet.getVisit(visitId) (VisitController.java findBookedVisit, Pet.java `if (!visit.isNew() && Objects.equals(visit.getId(), id))`), so a visit id belonging to another pet or owner is refused with IllegalArgumentException before any binding reaches a save; tests cover GET and POST foreign-visit and unknown-visit cases with `should(never()).save(any())`.

Mass assignment strengthened, not weakened: the @InitBinder keeps `dataBinder.setDisallowedFields("id", "*.id")` and adds `dataBinder.setAllowedFields("date", "description")`. The un-named @InitBinder applies to every binder in the controller, including the `@ModelAttribute Owner owner` parameter on both POST handlers, so request parameters can no longer bind Owner fields or nested `pets[...]` paths on visit routes; this closes a pre-existing over-binding reach on the booking route rather than introducing one.

Persisted-type binding is safe here because binding is bounded to the two form fields by the allow-list and the bound Visit carries @Valid; failed validation returns before owners.save, and `spring.jpa.open-in-view=false` (application.properties:11) keeps the loaded entity detached, so a rejected correction cannot flush.
Cross-request trust: each request re-resolves owner, pet, and visit from the URL in the @ModelAttribute method; nothing relies on prior-request validation (security-principles § Trust Boundaries).

Error disclosure: the new exception message carries only integer path ids (`"Visit with id " + visitId + " not found for pet with id " + pet.getId()`), mirroring the existing owner/pet refusal; visitId is typed Integer by path conversion, so no attacker text reaches the rendered error page.

Output escaping: the template is unchanged and `grep -rn "th:utext\|__\${" src/main/resources/templates` returned no hits, so visit description stays escaped by Thymeleaf defaults; no shell, file, query-concatenation, or deserialization sinks in the diff.
No secrets added: diff reviewed for credential-like literals; only test constants (descriptions, dates, ids).

Supply chain: no build file in the change set; OWASP dependency-check is not configured in build.gradle (`grep -n "dependencyCheck\|owasp" build.gradle` no hits) so no NVD match ran; resolved runtimeClasspath shows spring-boot 4.1.1, spring-webmvc 7.0.9, tools.jackson.core:jackson-databind 3.1.5.

Unauthenticated, CSRF-free mutating routes are the recorded demonstration baseline (security-principles § What this application is; system-design Threat Model row 1) and are not raised; the new edit route pair stays within that baseline and is recorded in the Threat Model mass-assignment row.
